generation: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production material/sprite sheet for an existing medieval pixel-art ruin dungeon, whose current screenshot is too visually busy and hard to read. The attached old masonry face is a STYLE REFERENCE only. Create ONE sheet exactly THREE equal columns by TWO equal rows, wide 1536x1024 if possible. SIX assets, one centered per equal cell with clean gutters. Maintain chunky medium-simple pixel art, game-ready dark outlines, muted natural materials and a flat orthographic x/y game grid. Improve readability: floors are QUIET and low-contrast, walls are solid and unmistakably raised, no distracting ivy or dense cracks on every surface. First row left: OPAQUE square texture of pale warm-grey worn large stone slabs for indoor ruined rooms; sparse hairline cracks, broad simple flat areas, subtle variation, no moss, no rubble or decoration, no border. First row middle: OPAQUE square texture of outdoor courtyard earth with muted olive grass/moss patches, natural and clearly distinct from the stone room floor; broad quiet pixel clusters, no stones or props. First row right: OPAQUE square texture of weathered grey paving with earth joints and only a little moss for clearly defined courtyard paths; quieter and less busy than a cobblestone mosaic, no border. Second row left: OPAQUE square top-facing wall-cap masonry texture of substantial dark slate-grey cut blocks with dark mortar and restrained highlights, unmistakably darker than room slabs, no ivy, no transparent holes. Second row middle: wide horizontal front-facing thick ruined stone wall strip, width440 height220, substantial solid grey blocks, strong dark crevices/outlines, a few chipped top stones and sparse moss; visibly raised wall face, no windows or household decor. No text, labels, characters, cast shadows or isometric camera. Original art. Limit fussy detail, fewer cracks, no noisy dithering. Keep pixel-art consistency with supplied masonry.
